item.title: Surviving the Antarctic: thermal tolerance adjustment in an invasive population of Psychoda albipennis (Zetterstedt, 1850)
item.description:
相关度 60.0 · 关键词匹配：biological invasion、climate change

Biological invasions in polar ecosystems are an increasing concern under climate change and intensifying human activity. We compared two geographically distant populations of the invasive dipteran Psychoda albipennis (Maritime Antarctica and the Magellanic sub-Antarctic) to assess population-level variation in lower and upper thermal tolerance. We further contextualized these responses through an exploratory comparison with published thermal-tolerance data for the non-native Trichocera maculipennis and the native Parochlus steinenii . item.description:
相关度 75.5 · 关键词匹配：climatic niche、climate change、protected area

Understanding vegetation responses to climatic variability is essential for anticipating future trajectories and informing management and conservation. Climatic niche metrics can improve climatic impact assessments by accounting for species‐specific climatic requirements. We analysed vegetation responses to gradual changes in climatic conditions in the monte blanco shrubland of Doñana National Park (SW Spain), one of Europe's most biodiverse protected areas. Specifically, we assessed vegetation dynamics over a 15‐year period (2007–2022) following a drought‐induced canopy loss event. We used species' climatic niche centroids as a proxy for their climatic optima and quantified their distance to observed climatic conditions as an indicator of climatic disequilibrium. item.title: Partitioning the variance of species–area relation into sampling‐ versus scale‐dependent components
item.description:
相关度 69.9 · 关键词匹配：species richness、uncertainty、spatial scale

The species–area relation (SAR) has been extensively studied over the past century, yet the sources of variation around an estimated SAR curve remain poorly understood. Here, we show that the sampling variance of the SAR can be decomposed into two additive components: 1) conditional variance, assuming that regional richness is fixed and represents uncertainty associated with local sampling; and 2) an additional component attributable to uncertainty in regional species richness, including uncertainty arising from rare species that remain undetected in the regional sample. We establish this decomposition mathematically and evaluate its behavior through numerical simulations. On this basis, empirical SAR observations can be classified as falling within the conditional confidence interval (CI), within the gap between the conditional and unconditional CIs, or outside the unconditional CI. Aim The Hutchinsonian shortfall, the lack of knowledge about species' abiotic tolerance, limits our understanding of species responses to environmental change and consequently also the outlining of their distribution in space and time. Such environmental tolerance is commonly inferred with two distinct approaches: i) trait performance studies, which use lab experiments to model species' functional responses, often overlooking real-world complexity, and ii) species distribution models, which infer environmental suitability from occurrence data, but offer limited causal insights. In this paper, we argue that these two strategies bring complementary information that can be integrated to estimate species-environment relationships more robustly and accurately map species distributions. item.title: Identifying key biodiversity areas in Mozambique for conservation planning and policy
item.description:
相关度 64.3 · 关键词匹配：conservation planning

The world is experiencing unprecedented rates of biodiversity loss. To reverse this trend, signatories to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) have committed to conserving at least 30% of marine and terrestrial areas by 2030, with an emphasis on sites critical for biodiversity. One mechanism to support this goal is the identification of Key Biodiversity Areas (KBAs) to inform spatial planning and the development of conservation area networks. However, few case studies demonstrate how the KBA process can be implemented in high-biodiversity, low-income countries. We present a national-scale example from Mozambique, where KBAs were delineated across seven taxonomic groups, and outline a post hoc theory of change to support broader national implementation and progress towards CBD targets. item.description:

Understanding how diversification dynamics interact with species traits and geographical distributions over time remains a central challenge in macroevolution and biogeography. Yet the timing of these associations is rarely tested explicitly: existing approaches often focus on present‐day trait–rate relationships, or summarize over the whole history of a clade, overlooking variations in historical processes acting over deep evolutionary timescales. item.title: Blueprints for restoration: Molecular monitoring and remote sensing support dispersal‐driven kelp recolonization
item.description:
相关度 64.3 · 关键词匹配：remote sensing

Nearshore marine habitats generate services worth billions of dollars, yet they are undergoing rapid, widespread degradation worldwide. Along northern California's coastline, a key habitat-forming annual species, bull kelp (Nereocystis luetkeana), has experienced historic declines of up to 95%. These losses have prompted efforts to uncover the mechanisms that influence kelp forest recovery, with the goal of restoring degraded habitats. Zoospore dispersal between neighboring populations is thought to be a key driver of recovery, yet the degree to which spore supply limits recolonization remains unresolved. A long-standing debate centers on whether persistent "gametophyte banks" fuel post-disturbance regrowth or whether recovery depends primarily on newly settled zoospores. To address this question, we combined high-resolution PlanetScope satellite imagery with molecular quantification of…

Methods We sampled bryophyte communities on three substrates (trees, rocks, and logs) across 54 sites on and near the northern and eastern shores of Lake Superior. item.title: Beaver Impacts Tool: A Graphical User Interface for Analyzing Ecosystem Impacts of Beaver Dams Using Remote Sensing Data
item.description:
相关度 64.3 · 关键词匹配：remote sensing

Beavers are being increasingly recognized as driving factors in diverse and resilient riparian ecosystems. Many of their impacts, including changes to water levels and vegetation, can be studied through remote sensing. However, ecologists and conservationists may lack the tools to easily analyze remote sensing data for these purposes. We offer here a Google Earth Engine-backed Streamlit app that allows users to easily upload locations of observed dams or installed beaver dam analogs for analysis. Via a graphical user interface, users then generate a set of dam-absent locations for comparison and receive plots and numerical data indicating how indices associated with vegetation, water, temperature, and evapotranspiration change over time for dam-present and dam-absent locations. Based on the availability of open datasets, our tool provides coverage from 2017 onward. The cloud version of…

item.description:
相关度 76.7 · 关键词匹配：species distribution modelling、range shift、climate change

Invasive tree pests and pathogens are increasingly threatening forests worldwide. Understanding how a warming climate and changing precipitation patterns will affect the future distribution ranges of these pathogenic species requires systematic analysis across a variety of host trees and pathogenic species. We analysed 31 major tree pests and pathogens that have caused widespread and extensive damage globally, predicting their current and future distribution under various climate change scenarios using species distribution modelling. Our results showed that tree pests and pathogens will consistently shift northward, threatening northern temperate and boreal forests between the years 2041 and 2080. Protected areas face increasing challenges due to climate change and land-use transformations, prompting the need for complementary conservation strategies such as sacred natural sites. Sacred natural sites, valued for their cultural and spiritual significance, historically harbor rich biodiversity and provide key ecosystem services. We investigate the distribution and conservation relevance of sacred natural sites in Pantanal lowlands and surrounding highlands plateau, the Cerrado, two biologically diverse regions that form the upper Paraguay River basin in Brazil. Based on the understanding that landscape features influence both ecological processes and cultural practices, we analyzed the spatial congruence between sacred natural sites, ecological corridors, and Priority Resilience Climate Change Areas. Aims Data from participatory science projects are widely used to understand species distributions. However, participatory science data often contain biases that can obscure real patterns. We address two sources of sampling bias: location uncertainty of individual records and spatially heterogeneous sampling effort. A variety of data processing and modelling strategies have been used to address these biases, without consensus on their relative effectiveness. We test several strategies using data from iNaturalist, a large repository of participatory science data. item.description:

Protected areas (PAs) are central to biodiversity conservation, yet their capacity to buffer species from climate‐driven heat exposure, that is, the duration and frequency of exposure to temperatures exceeding species' critical thermal limits, remains poorly quantified at global scales. Here, we assessed whether squamate reptiles inside PAs experience lower heat exposure than conspecifics in unprotected, human‐modified landscapes, and how this buffering effect varies across latitudes, biomes, and evolutionary lineages. Using biophysical modelling of operative temperatures across 248 species, we show that PAs consistently reduced both annual hours above critical thermal maximum (CT max ) and the frequency of critical days under current and future climatic scenarios (+2°C and + 4°C). Climate change is expected to drive substantial shifts in species distributions, yet ecological responses are often delayed under disequilibrium dynamics, limiting the effectiveness of range‐based indicators for detecting ongoing change. Compositional approaches have been proposed as an alternative; however, conventional comparisons based on gradient shape or pointwise differences may fail to detect change when the overall gradient structure is conserved, because small and spatially heterogeneous differences cancel out across the gradient. Here, we address this limitation by presenting a direction‐sensitive analytical framework that integrates signed differences along environmental gradients. item.title: Migrant frugivorous birds assist plants in tracking climate change: A first spatially explicit approach
item.description:
相关度 68.2 · 关键词匹配：species distribution model、climatic suitability、dispersal model

Climate change is causing biodiversity redistributions towards cooler areas at an unprecedented velocity. Plants are an essential component of terrestrial ecosystems that primarily rely on seed dispersal to redistribute. Yet, most seed dispersal occurs over short distances (i.e. less than 1 km), which is insufficient to track ongoing climate change. Bird migration can support seed dispersal at longer distances. However, we lack spatially explicit estimations of seed dispersal by migratory birds towards future climatically suitable ranges of plants. Thereby, it remains unclear to what extent they can facilitate plant redistribution in the coming decades. We integrated spatially explicit, seed‐dispersal models with projections on plant climatic suitability using species distribution models. item.description:

The theory of island biogeography (TIB) explains species richness patterns, yet its extension to compositional dissimilarity (β diversity), particularly from multidimensional perspectives, remains limited. Using butterfly assemblages across 44 land‐bridge islands in the Zhoushan Archipelago, China, we applied an integrative framework to unravel how island geography and species traits shape multi‐faceted β diversity. We partitioned taxonomic, phylogenetic, and functional β diversity into turnover and nestedness components, quantified species and site contributions, and distinguished roles of widespread versus restricted species. Planting seedlings beyond a species’ or population’s current distribution is a potential management strategy to help plants keep pace with changing climate. The extent to which both climate of origin and spatial climate differences affect seedling traits such as biomass allocation, however, remains poorly understood. Sugar maple ( Acer saccharum ) seedlings from three USA source populations with contrasting climates (from south to north; Missouri, Iowa, Minnesota) were grown for three years at nine forested sites, from Arkansas, USA, to Ontario, Canada, to test hypotheses about ecotypic and biogeographic variation in root biomass fraction (RMF, assessed herein with root biomass/[root biomass + stem biomass]). Global warming is rapidly restructuring biological communities, yet terrestrial ecosystems often appear to lack the systematic climate‐driven signatures observed in marine realms. We hypothesise that this apparent idiosyncrasy arises from neglecting the geographic structure of climate. Using 1161 terrestrial community time series, we transitioned from geographic grids to a multidimensional climate space defined by temperature and precipitation. This framework allows climatic associations to be evaluated while accounting for climate‐space geometry by quantifying two key components: climate area and climate isolation. item.description:

Elephants and other megaherbivores can strongly modify woody vegetation, yet their influence across heterogeneous landscapes and spatial scales remains poorly resolved. Here, we combined remotely sensed time series of vegetation height (2000–2022) and woody cover (2015–2025) with elephant population counts from 34 reserves across eight southern African countries to investigate the relationship between elephants and woody vegetation dynamics at local and landscape scales. To represent uneven within‐reserve use, we further used movement data from 315 GPS‐collared elephants to model habitat selection and estimate spatially explicit local densities in 15 reserves. However, the reliability of these inferences has rarely been systematically evaluated, particularly with respect to their sensitivity to individual occurrences. Here, we used virtual species and developed a sample perturbations diagnostic framework, in which each occurrence was systematically removed (leave‐one‐out) to assess how small changes in the input data affect variable importance inference. In the American continent, they have a complex biogeographical history, shaped by processes of colonization and adaptive radiation that have generated a high diversity of lineages. However, under the global biodiversity crisis, this group faces increasing extinction risk, and conservation efforts have focused mainly on species richness while neglecting evolutionary relationships. item.description:

The metabolic theory of ecology (MTE) conceptualizes that temperature is the primary driver of species richness, a pattern well supported in terrestrial taxa but less certain for freshwater organisms. Limited global‐scale evidence and frequent violations of MTE's assumptions, particularly regarding the stationarity of body size and abundance, further undermine its applicability. In freshwater systems, body size and abundance are tightly linked to dispersal and range size, which differ markedly between running‐water (lotic) and standing‐water (lentic) species, as proposed by the Habitat‐Stability–Dispersal Hypothesis (HSDH). Adaptations to habitat stability may therefore generate distinct biogeographical patterns of traits and modify richness–temperature relationships predicted by MTE. item.description:

Understanding how anthropogenic pressures and environmental gradients shape coastal fish communities is a central question in biogeography and marine conservation. Yet, the set of species expected to occur at a site given ecological conditions but being absent – the so‐called dark diversity – has received far less attention than observed species, even if they hold key information about local extirpations and conservation effectiveness. Quantifying dark diversity in the sea is particularly challenging because many species are rare, cryptobenthic or mobile, while sampling effort is rarely standardized. Here we combined 930 environmental DNA (eDNA) samples collected at 401 sites along 2000 km of the French Mediterranean coast with fine‐scale mapping of habitats, anthropogenic pressures and protection levels. item.description:

Systematic conservation planning provides a science‐based framework for defining conservation goals and supporting transparent spatial decision‐making under limited resources. Within this framework, spatial conservation prioritisation tools are widely used to identify areas of high biodiversity value by integrating information on species distributions, connectivity, costs, and other factors into spatially explicit recommendations. ‘Zonation' is one of the leading software tools in this field, producing hierarchical priority rankings of landscapes based on conservation value. However, its standard workflow typically relies on manual steps for data preparation, execution, and post‐processing, which can become inefficient and difficult to reproduce when multiple scenarios are analysed, limiting accessibility and broader uptake. item.title: Predicting Red List categories reveals hidden extinction risk in one of the world’s most diverse freshwater invertebrate families
item.description:
相关度 66.2 · 关键词匹配：risk assessment、extinction risk、geographic range

Global Red List assessments suggest that approximately 25% of freshwater animal species are at risk of extinction. However, these estimates remain tentative due to insufficient assessments of numerous species-rich invertebrate groups in neglected ecosystems, such as springs and subterranean waters.
